lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Replace the portfolio URL with a real, accessible repository or portfolio link.
items.because: The current URL looks like a placeholder.

items.says: Consider adding a current LinkedIn, Google Scholar, GitHub, or personal research page.
items.because: A repository, working-paper page, or publication profile may be more useful for quant research roles.

items.says: Verify that “Ph.D. candidate” matches the program’s formal candidacy status.
items.because: The title is appropriate only after reaching candidacy under the program’s definition.

items.says: Add a relevant research specialization.
items.because: It would help recruiters understand the fit with financial econometrics, time-series modeling, statistical learning, or high-dimensional statistics.

items.says: Consider adding a dissertation title, dissertation status, or expected defense timing if useful.
items.because: That detail could strengthen research-oriented applications.

items.says: Ensure the expected May 2026 completion date is current.
items.because: Any changed completion date should be updated consistently.

items.says: Consider adding honors, GPA, or relevant coursework only if strong and useful.
items.because: The older undergraduate degree is less important than the graduate experience.

items.says: Consider shortening the education section if space is tight.
items.because: The Ph.D. is the more important credential for quant and research positions.

items.says: Check whether the September 2025 start date and “Present” status are accurate for when the résumé is used.
items.because: “Present” may be inaccurate if the résumé is used before or shortly after September 2025.

items.says: Clarify if the bakery position is a secondary job held while finishing the Ph.D.
items.because: That context is not currently clear.

items.says: Reduce the bakery role’s prominence or place it under “Additional Experience.”
items.because: It demonstrates transferable responsibility but is not directly relevant to quant research.

items.says: Change “labour” to “labor.”
items.because: That spelling is more consistent with the U.S. location and the rest of the résumé.

items.says: Quantify the budget’s scale or outcome if it can be substantiated.
items.because: Keeping the store within budget does not currently show the scale or result.

items.says: Fix the awkward line wrapping around “labour budget.”
items.because: The bullet should remain easy to scan.

items.says: Clarify the period and measurement basis for the reduction from 12% to 7%.
items.because: “Unsold bread” could refer to units, value, or production volume.

items.says: Make clear that “production” and “unsold bread” use a consistent denominator.
items.because: The measurement basis must be clear for the reduction to be credible.

items.says: Define the specific metric meant by “risk-adjusted returns.”
items.because: The phrase is vague and could mean Sharpe ratio, information ratio, drawdown-adjusted return, or another measure.

items.says: Clarify whether the 35% improvement is relative or percentage-point and give its period, benchmark, and cost assumptions.
items.because: Without that context, the number is difficult to interpret.

items.says: Distinguish whether the reported improvement was simulated, paper, or live performance.
items.because: The wording should not imply live performance if it was only a backtest.

items.says: Clarify how the position-smoother result differs from the final Northpeak futures-signal result.
items.because: The two bullets currently look overlapping or contradictory.

items.says: Shorten the explanation after “so” and focus on the methodological safeguard.
items.because: The explanation of basic logic is somewhat long despite the useful technical terms.

items.says: Specify the tick data’s asset class, instruments, and approximate observation scale if permitted.
items.because: “Six years of tick data” does not fully convey the data scope.

items.says: Fix the awkward line wrapping around “embargo period.”
items.because: The bullet should remain easy to scan.

items.says: Clarify whether the feature store was deployed or adopted rather than merely available.
items.because: The claim that it was reused in two later projects should accurately describe the contribution.

items.says: Verify the live-allocation claim and specify exactly what the portfolio managers approved.
items.because: “Approved” is a strong claim and could refer to the signal, the recommendation, or a broader strategy.

items.says: Selecting the best of 400 backtested configurations introduces multiple-testing and selection bias.
items.because: The procedure signals overfitting.

items.says: The best backtested Sharpe should not be reported as the expected live Sharpe.
items.because: That is an incorrect and overstated interpretation of the selected result.

items.says: Clarify how the order-book imbalance result differs from the earlier Northpeak position-smoother result.
items.because: Both bullets describe a cost-aware futures strategy and Sharpe improvement, making them look overlapping or contradictory.

items.says: The order-book imbalance result duplicates the Kaggle futures-signal result.
items.because: The same Sharpe increase over 18 months looks copied, misattributed, or factually inconsistent.

items.says: Use “out of sample” only if the model and all decisions were frozen before the evaluation period.
items.because: An 18-month historical evaluation is not necessarily out of sample, and it is not 18 months of live results from a three-month internship.

items.says: Add context on realistic costs, turnover, capacity, and the statistical or economic meaning of the Sharpe increase.
items.because: The raw improvement is not fully supported by the current context.

items.says: Fix the awkward wrapping of the final Northpeak bullet.
items.because: The bullet should remain easy to scan.

items.says: Using the same random seed on every worker is not an appropriate implementation of independent Monte Carlo simulation.
items.because: It can produce identical or correlated simulations and undermine the study’s validity.

items.says: Clarify whether the reduction from three days to five hours refers to wall-clock time or total compute time.
items.because: Parallelization can reduce elapsed time while increasing total compute.

items.says: Describe the log-factor improvement as a theorem, corollary, or empirical observation, as appropriate.
items.because: The mathematical nature of the theoretical contribution is not precise.

items.says: Ensure that “under review at JASA” is true and does not imply acceptance or publication.
items.because: Submission status must be handled carefully.

items.says: Add the evaluation instrument and approximate response count for the 4.8/5 rating if known.
items.because: Those details would improve the rating’s credibility.

items.says: Clarify whether the R package is still maintained.
items.because: Maintenance is relevant evidence for technical roles.

items.says: Consider adding verifiable evidence such as documentation, tests, citations, or institutional adoption.
items.because: Those measures may be more relevant than download count alone.

items.says: Specify the forecast horizon, evaluation design, and whether the 7% QLIKE improvement is relative or absolute.
items.because: The meaning of “beat” is currently underspecified.

items.says: Clarify that the test period was separated and was not used for tuning.
items.because: The “out-of-sample” claim requires a genuinely untouched test period.

items.says: State whether the result across 30 indices is an average, median, pooled result, or another aggregate.
items.because: Results can be dominated by a few indices or by differing sample lengths.

items.says: Ensure that “held at the 5% level” accurately describes the tested hypothesis and Holm correction.
items.because: The significance wording must match the exact procedure.

items.says: Avoid implying that statistical significance establishes economic usefulness.
items.because: A significant forecast gain is not necessarily economically useful.

items.says: Name or define the two crisis periods.
items.because: The periods are not obvious from the résumé.

items.says: Clarify that the crisis periods were not selected after examining many candidate subperiods.
items.because: Post-selection would weaken the crisis-period claim.

items.says: Add a repository or paper link if available.
items.because: Allowing reviewers to inspect the work would increase the project’s value.

items.says: Verify that “working paper” is the correct status.
items.because: A class or seminar paper should be labeled accurately.

items.says: Add the competition name and a strong placement or score if available.
items.because: “Market prediction competition” is generic and does not establish the outcome.

items.says: Clarify the individual contribution within the three-person Kaggle project.
items.because: The bullets do not make clear which parts were personally implemented.

items.says: Make the feature-engineering and gradient-boosting bullet more specific or remove it.
items.because: It is generic and lacks concrete scope or outcome.

items.says: Explain what caused the validation–leaderboard gap and how the revised folds were shown to reduce leakage.
items.because: Changing the evaluation distribution alone would not establish that leakage was reduced.

items.says: The futures-signal result duplicates the Northpeak order-book imbalance result.
items.because: The nearly identical Sharpe increase and 18-month period make the résumé look padded, misattributed, or inconsistent.

items.says: State the baseline, costs, turnover, evaluation period, and whether the Sharpe increase was simulated or live.
items.because: A raw Sharpe increase without context can look like backtest overfitting.

items.says: Order the programming skills by proficiency and relevance.
items.because: The strongest and most role-relevant tools should appear first.

items.says: Consider adding demonstrated tools such as SQL, Git, Linux, cloud infrastructure, distributed computing, or specific data libraries.
items.because: Relevant tools used in the work are missing from the skills list.

items.says: Clarify the role of Kafka or remove it.
items.because: Kafka appears nowhere else and may invite questions about the depth of experience.

items.says: Correct “econometircs” to “econometrics.”
items.because: A typo in a core quantitative method is especially damaging.

items.says: Use consistent capitalization and precise terminology for the listed methods.
items.because: The labels should accurately reflect the training.

items.says: Consider adding demonstrated methods such as Monte Carlo, volatility modeling, statistical testing, and walk-forward validation.
items.because: The methods section does not reflect several of the résumé’s strongest technical areas.

items.says: List only methods that can be defended technically.
items.because: The backtesting and multiple-testing issues may prompt detailed interview questions.

items.says: Consider adding a publications or research section.
items.because: The theorem, JASA submission, R package, and working paper may deserve greater visibility.

items.says: Tailor the section emphasis to the target role.
items.because: Quant, general data-science, and academic roles prioritize different parts of the résumé.
